subject: Are regression diagnostics possible/necessary in lavaan?

messages.author: 133d81adf36adb07
messages.subject: Are regression diagnostics possible/necessary in lavaan?
parts:
Hello lavaan-community!


I'm doing a mediation analysis with the "sem"-function in lavaan. Since the process is regression-based i thought that regression diagnostics (e.g. test of normal distribution of residuals) would be necessary. But functions that are normally used for this kind of diagnostics from the "car"-package don't work in Lavaan. I've looked into this, but found no information relating to regression diagnostics in SEM - which led me to believe that it might not be necessary. Does anybody know for sure?


I am a psychology student and structural equation models are just finding their way in to psychological studies, so it is hard to find straight answers at my university.


Any help would be much appreciated.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Are regression diagnostics possible/necessary in lavaan?
parts:
Patricia--
     If you are doing a mediation analysis using common factors, then common regression residual diagnostics are impossible because common factors are indeterminate functions of the data. In regression, residuals can be computed as determinate functions of the observed variables and the parameter estimates. Bollen and Arminger (1991) discussed observation residuals in SEM, but did so using "regression method" factor scores, which are not actually identical with the common factors.

 Bollen, K. A., & Arminger, G. (1991). Observational residuals in factor analysis and structural equation models. Sociological methodology, 235-262.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Are regression diagnostics possible/necessary in lavaan?
parts: That is not correct. ML estimation requires multivariate normality. Multinormality means that higher order moments of the data beyond the second can be computed from lower order moments, so that a covariance matrix in itself is a sufficient statistic. Other estimators for structural equation models do not require multinormality. So the distributional requirement is tied to the estimator, not to the form of the model, or even to the use of common factors rather than, say, composites, to represent the unobserved variables.
